title: v1/chat.completions: robust param coercion, stop/logprob envelope, functioncall handshake, and stream jitter mitigation
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Bring Redwood's /v1/chat.completions adapter closer to OpenAI parity while improving real-world stability for streaming and function/tool calling. This PR consolidates several interrelated fixes: 1) resilient parameter coercion and normalization for v1 inputs (temperature, top_p, stop as mixed types, role aliases), 2) move per-token logprob payloads into a stable envelope to avoid interleaving with delta tokens, 3) add an explicit functioncall handshake frame and deterministic tool-call framing for mixed streaming and non-streaming flows, 4) implement stream jitter mitigation and backpressure heuristics to reduce visible client-side reflow and duplicate partial tokens. Summary of changes: input layer: added a coercion/validation pass that accepts numeric strings for temperature/top_p, truncates extreme values to safe ranges, accepts stop as string or array or array-of-mixed, and emits canonical stop arrays; role normalization: map common role aliases and enforce precedence rules (system > user > assistant) to avoid prompt inversion bugs; streaming: introduce HEARTBEAT frames and a pacing layer that enforces a token inter-arrival smoothing algorithm (configurable via environment flag REDWOOD_STREAM_PACE_MS) and a high-water/low-water backpressure window to avoid buffering storms on slow clients; logprobs: decouple logprob data into a sibling envelope field "logprob_delta" that is only emitted when present to avoid JSON parse ambiguity in streaming clients; functioncall/tooling: introduce a 2-step handshake (FUNCTIONCALL_OFFER -> FUNCTIONCALL_ACK) when the adapter intends to forward tool calls to a downstream tool runner; tool outputs are wrapped in assistant.tools array with explicit metadata (tool_name, status, raw_output) so client SDKs can reliably detect structured tool results; compatibility: add heuristics for common OpenAI v1 mis-use (e.g., stop: null, temperature: "0.0") and emit deprecation warnings in the response metadata instead of hard errors where safe. Testing & stability: added deterministic unit tests for role/stop normalization, integration tests that exercise streamed functioncall sequences with intermittent connection loss, and a stress test for the pacing/backpressure logic. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag (compat_v1_relaxed_coercion=true) with a canary on 10% of hosted traffic for 48h, full rollout contingent on no regressions in CANARY_STREAM_LATENCY and no increase in token duplication errors. Checklist: - [x] implement param coercion and role normalization - [x] implement logprob envelope and streaming-safe framing - [x] add functioncall handshake and tool output envelope - [x] add pacing/backpressure module and feature flag - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] update adapter docs and changelog - [x] run canary and monitor metrics Backwards compatibility notes: default behavior preserves existing semantics unless the compat flag is enabled. Some edge-case clients relying on interleaved logprob deltas will need to opt-in to parsing the new envelope. Monitoring & observability: emit new metrics: stream.pacing.delays, stream.backpressure.trips, adapter.v1.coercion_warnings, functioncall.handshakes.total, functioncall.handshakes.failed. Security: no changes to auth surface. Performance: pacing slightly increases median tail by configurable ms but reduces duplication and re-transmit work overall. See release notes below for suggested migration steps.
commits: feat(adapter): add v1 param coercion and role normalization
feat(stream): add heartbeat frames and pacing/backpressure layer
feat(functions): introduce functioncall handshake and tool output envelope
chore(tests): add unit/integration tests for v1 compat and stream stability
docs(adapter): document v1 compatibility flag and examples
review_comments: Ethan Zhao: Left a note about making the pacing window size configurable per-route; let's avoid global defaults for large tenants.
Maya Patel: Can we ensure the functioncall handshake tolerates idempotent replays? Add a request-id for dedupe.
Sofia Ruiz: Integration tests flaked on CI initially due to timer sensitivity; reworked tests to use fake clock. Approving after that change.
release_notes: Compatibility: Add optional relaxed v1 coercion to accept common OpenAI parameter shapes and role aliases. Streaming: introduce heartbeat frames and pacing/backpressure to mitigate jitter and duplicate tokens. Function calling: new 2-step handshake and explicit tool output envelope for deterministic downstream execution. Note: clients relying on interleaved logprob deltas must update to parse the new logprob envelope when the compat flag is enabled.
